comments.content:
Faisal Khatri Michelle Obama did not just "follow" the guidelines from the tune —she actively changed and modernized them. Through the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010, her initiative updated school meal standards for the first time in 30 years to better align with contemporary dietary science.The Let's Move! initiative created strict new rules for federally subsidized school lunches. These changes required schools to: Increase servings of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Require students to take a fruit or vegetable with their meal. Restrict calories, trans fats, and sodium levels. Limit flavored milk to fat-free options.
While these new standards successfully improved the nutritional quality of meals, they faced major backlash from critics who argued the strict rules led to higher costs, "plate waste" where kids threw food away, and lower school lunch participation rates. This opposition eventually prompted the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) under subsequent administrations to ease some of the strictest whole-grain and sodium limits.
